edits.line: The bag costs EUR 80. Shipping charges are shown at checkout, so you can see them as you move through the purchase path.
edits.problem: The only practical reason to return—the opportunity to reveal the remaining shipping cost before deciding—is described passively instead of being connected to the click.
edits.fix: Make clear that resuming checkout lets the reader see the shipping charge and then decide, without implying that the basket immediately shows a final delivered total.

edits.line: If you would like to continue deciding, the basket is the place to pick up again.
edits.problem: This merely explains what a basket is and adds no reason to click before the CTA repeats the same instruction.
edits.fix: Remove the sentence so the opening moves directly from recognizing the abandoned item to the documented price and checkout disclosure.

edits.line: You can return when you’re ready, look over what is in your basket, and decide whether you want to complete the purchase. This reminder is simply a way back to the choice you had already started considering, in your own time.
edits.problem: The closing restates the same permission and decision several times, which caused attention to expire before the CTA.
edits.fix: Condense the closing to one direct transition into the single basket CTA, preserving the unhurried tone without repeating the proposition.

summary: Make the shipping disclosure the concrete payoff of returning, then cut the repeated explanations so the reader reaches the basket link promptly.
